scenes.heading: Getting your first paying clients before you have testimonials

sents.d: Getting your first paying clients before you have testimonials
Discounted pilot clients can generate the proof you need to charge full price later.

Without testimonials or case studies, new coaches and consultants often struggle to justify their asking price to skeptical prospects — offering a small number of discounted 'pilot' spots in exchange for detailed testimonials and honest feedback solves this early gap.

Existing personal and professional networks are an underused first client source — letting people know specifically what you now offer, rather than a vague 'I'm coaching now' announcement, makes it much easier for them to refer you or become clients themselves.

Offering a single, well-structured free or low-cost session (not an ongoing free relationship) to a handful of ideal-fit prospects can convert into paying engagements once they experience your actual approach directly.

take: Use pilot clients and your network to earn your first testimonials.
